summary: Renal-transplant recipient on tacrolimus and prednisolone with a penicillin allergy: antibiotics now indicated (non-penicillin regimen) and admission favoured.

inputs.hpi: Two days of constant left iliac fossa pain with mild nausea; eating and drinking. Renal transplant 2019 on tacrolimus and prednisolone.

exam.abdomen: Tender left iliac fossa with mild localised guarding; no peritonism, no mass.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis
imaging.result: Uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis (modified Hinchey Ia): pericolic fat stranding; no abscess, no free gas, no free fluid.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute uncomplicated diverticulitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: CT-confirmed uncomplicated sigmoid diverticulitis in an immunosuppressed transplant recipient.

match: re:penicillin allergy recorded raised the harm of antibiotics

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — acute colonic diverticulitis (2020 update)
guideline.section: Uncomplicated diverticulitis: antibiotics and outpatient management
guideline.citation: Sartelli M et al. World J Emerg Surg 2020;15:32.

guideline.name: DIABOLO trial
guideline.citation: Daniels L et al. Br J Surg 2017;104:52-61.

rationale: Immunocompromised patients were excluded from the trials of observation; WSES 2020 advises antibiotics (and a low threshold for admission) in immunosuppression. The allergy class directs a non-penicillin regimen.
